title: Assetto AI Director style profile
description:
A directorial style: how fast to cut, how to distribute camera behaviour, and how to value each moment. Authored as TOML — a style is meant to be read, edited and reviewed by a person, and to sit in version control where a diff shows what someone changed about the look of a cut. This schema describes the parsed document, since TOML shares JSON's data model; validate a profile by parsing it and checking the result against this file. A test does exactly that for every built-in style and every shipped profile.

The defining feature is that every tunable carries its provenance. A number cannot gain authority merely by being written down: a value declared measured must name where it was measured from, and the shorthand for a bare number resolves to a guess, never to something stronger.

schema_version.description: Bumped when the file shape changes incompatibly, so a reader can refuse rather than misinterpret.

description.description: Human-readable summary of what this style looks like.

seed.description: Seed for the rhythm generator, so an edit is reproducible.

measured_from.description: Reference clips this profile's numbers were measured from. Empty for a hand-authored profile — and a profile claiming measured provenance with nothing here is a profile whose claim cannot be checked.

rhythm.description: How this style paces its cutting.

median_shot_length.description: Target median shot duration, seconds. Median, not mean, and the distinction is load-bearing: measured shot-length distributions are strongly right-skewed and sometimes bimodal. One reference clip has a 6.11 s mean against a 2.23 s median, because it is mostly short shots punctuated by a few very long ones — targeting the mean there would produce an edit resembling neither.

spread.description: Coefficient of variation, sigma over mu. Scale-free, so it transfers between a fast style and a slow one.

spectral_slope.description: Target log-log slope of the shot-length sequence. Zero is white noise — independent lengths, which real editing is not. Around minus one is the pink-noise structure observed in film.

min_shot_length.description: Floor, below which a shot cannot be read.

max_shot_length.description: Ceiling, above which a shot outstays its welcome.

camera_mix.description: How this style distributes camera behaviour across shots. Fractions are targets rather than quotas: the scheduler weights candidate generation by them, but geometric feasibility can still override. A trackside camera that cannot see the car is not placed merely to hit a percentage — so these need not sum to one, and a validator must not require it.

static_fraction.description: Share of shots that should be locked off.

axial_fraction.description: Share travelling along the optical axis — chase, bonnet, bumper, follow-drone.

track_fraction.description: Share translating laterally alongside the subject.

allowed_rigs.description: Rigs this style permits at all. A style that forbids drones says so here rather than through a zero weight, so an unsatisfiable request fails loudly instead of silently drifting. Absent means all rigs are permitted.

weights.description: How this style values each moment score. These are the one part of a profile that is deliberately NOT provenance-tracked: they are editorial judgement, not measurement, and wrapping them in a tunable would let them appear in the provenance report as though they were evidence. The report names them explicitly as untracked instead.

tunable.description: A number and where it came from. The bare-number form is shorthand for a guess — hand-editing a profile to try a value should not require writing a provenance block, but the shorthand can only ever resolve to GUESS, so convenience cannot launder an unsourced number into a measured one.

provenance.description: verified: read from a primary source or the game's own data. measured: produced by this project's measurement harness from named footage. derived: computed from other tracked values. guess: judgement, and counted as such by CI.

source.description: Where the value came from. Required for anything other than a guess — a non-guess without a source is rejected at construction, because an unsourced claim of authority is the exact failure this type exists to prevent.

note.description: Anything a later reader needs in order to judge the value.
